description: Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted is a majestic centerpiece, perfect for grand celebrations. This traditional Middle Eastern dish features a whole lamb, meticulously marinated and slow-roasted until incredibly tender, falling off the bone. It's often served atop a fragrant bed of spiced rice, garnished with nuts, creating an unforgettable culinary experience that embodies hospitality and rich flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare the Lamb Marinade
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, 4 tablespoons of mixed spice, cumin, coriander, paprika, turmeric, black pepper, and 3 tablespoons of salt. Mix well to form a thick paste.

instructions.title: Marinate the Lamb
instructions.text: Pat the whole lamb dry with paper towels. Make several deep incisions all over the lamb with a sharp knife. Rub the prepared marinade generously over the entire lamb, ensuring it penetrates the incisions. Place quartered onions and bay leaves inside the cavity. Cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, or preferably 24 hours, to allow flavors to meld.

instructions.title: Prepare the Ouzi Rice
instructions.text: Melt ghee or butter in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté the finely chopped onions until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add ground lamb or beef and cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon. Stir in 2 tablespoons of mixed spice, cinnamon powder, cardamom powder, 2 teaspoons of salt, and 1 teaspoon of black pepper. Add the soaked and drained basmati rice, stirring to coat evenly with the spices and meat. Pour in chicken or lamb broth, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes until the rice is almost cooked and liquid is absorbed. Stir in frozen peas and diced carrots (if using).

instructions.title: Stuff and Prepare for Roasting
instructions.text: Allow the cooked Ouzi rice to cool slightly. Carefully spoon the rice mixture into the lamb's cavity. Secure the opening with butcher's twine or skewers to keep the stuffing inside. Place the stuffed lamb on a large roasting rack set over a deep roasting pan. Add 2-3 cups of water to the bottom of the pan along with the cinnamon sticks to create a moist environment for roasting.

instructions.title: Slow Roast the Lamb
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 150°C (300°F). Cover the entire roasting pan tightly with heavy-duty aluminum foil, ensuring no steam escapes. This is crucial for tenderizing the lamb. Roast for 8-10 hours, or until the lamb is exceptionally tender and literally falling off the bone. You may baste occasionally with pan juices if desired, carefully re-covering each time.

instructions.title: Achieve Golden Finish
instructions.text: During the last 30-60 minutes of cooking, carefully remove the foil. Increase the oven temperature to 180°C (350°F) to allow the lamb skin to crisp and brown beautifully, giving it an appetizing golden color. Monitor closely to prevent any burning.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Carefully remove the lamb from the oven and let it rest for at least 30 minutes before carving. This allows the meat's juices to redistribute, ensuring maximum tenderness and flavor. Serve the whole roasted lamb on a grand platter, surrounded by any remaining Ouzi rice (if not fully used for stuffing) and garnished generously with toasted almonds, pine nuts, and fresh chopped parsley or mint.

tips: For the most authentic flavor and tenderness, allow the lamb to marinate for a full 24 hours in the refrigerator. This deepens the spice penetration and significantly tenderizes the meat.

If you don't have access to a whole lamb, this recipe can be adapted for a large lamb shoulder or leg. Adjust roasting time accordingly, typically 4-6 hours for a large cut, ensuring it reaches fall-off-the-bone tenderness.

To prevent the Ouzi rice from becoming mushy when stuffed inside the lamb, undercook it slightly (by a few minutes) before stuffing, as it will continue to cook and absorb flavors inside the lamb's cavity.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of the Middle East, where flavors are rich, aromas are intoxicating, and hospitality is paramount. At the center of many grand feasts lies a dish that embodies celebration and comfort: Lamb Ouzi Whole Slow Roasted. This magnificent centerpiece, with its fall-off-the-bone tender lamb and aromatic spiced rice, is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Perfect for special occasions or when you simply want to impress, this Middle Eastern dinner recipe promises a symphony of tastes that will transport your guests. Forget complicated techniques; the secret to this dish lies in patience and a commitment to slow roasting, allowing the lamb to develop an incredible depth of flavor.

## What is Lamb Ouzi?

Lamb Ouzi, often pronounced "Oozy," is a celebrated traditional Middle Eastern dish renowned for its impressive presentation and exquisite taste. While variations exist across the region, the essence remains the same: succulent, slow-cooked lamb served over a bed of fragrant, spiced rice, often studded with toasted nuts and sometimes peas. It's a dish typically reserved for significant gatherings, holidays, and family celebrations, symbolizing generosity and abundance.

The lamb component can range from a whole roasted lamb (especially for very large feasts) to a whole leg or shoulder of lamb, which is more practical for home cooks. The slow roasting process is crucial, breaking down tough fibers and rendering the meat incredibly tender and flavorful. The accompanying rice pilaf is equally important, infused with a medley of warm spices like cinnamon, cardamom, and allspice, creating a perfect counterpoint to the rich lamb. When you present a platter of Lamb Ouzi, you're not just serving food; you're sharing a piece of Middle Eastern culinary heritage.

## Ingredients for Whole Slow Roasted Lamb Ouzi

Crafting the perfect Lamb Ouzi requires a selection of quality ingredients that come together to create its signature taste.

**For the Lamb:**
*   **Whole Leg or Shoulder of Lamb:** 5-7 pounds, bone-in (for maximum flavor).
*   **Olive Oil:** 1/4 cup.
*   **Fresh Garlic:** 6-8 cloves, minced.
*   **Lemon Juice:** 1/4 cup.
*   **Spices for Marinade:** 2 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp ground cumin, 1 tbsp ground coriander, 1 tsp ground paprika, 1/2 tsp ground turmeric, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (optional, for a kick).
*   **Onions & Carrots (Optional):** 1 large onion, quartered; 2 carrots, roughly chopped, for the roasting pan to add flavor to drippings.
*   **Chicken or Vegetable Broth:** 2 cups, for the roasting pan.

**For the Aromatic Spiced Rice:**
*   **Basmati Rice:** 3 cups, rinsed thoroughly.
*   **Butter or Ghee:** 3 tbsp.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped.
*   **Whole Spices:** 4-5 green cardamom pods, 2 bay leaves, 1 cinnamon stick.
*   **Ground Spices:** 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1/2 tsp ground allspice, 1/2 tsp ground turmeric, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon.
*   **Chicken or Vegetable Broth:** 4 1/2 cups.
*   **Salt:** 1 tsp, or to taste.
*   **Frozen Peas:** 1 cup (optional).

**For Garnish:**
*   **Toasted Nuts:** 1/2 cup mixed (pine nuts, slivered almonds, pistachios).
*   **Fresh Parsley:** 1/4 cup, chopped.

## How to Make Lamb Ouzi: Step-by-Step Guide

Preparing this impressive whole slow roasted lamb dish is simpler than you might think, primarily requiring time and patience.

1.  **Prepare the Lamb:** Pat the lamb leg dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make several deep incisions all over the lamb. In a small bowl, whisk together the olive oil, minced garlic, lemon juice, and all the lamb marinade spices. Generously rub this mixture all over the lamb, ensuring it gets into the incisions. For best results, place the lamb in a large roasting pan, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours, or ideally overnight. Bring to room temperature for about an hour before roasting.

2.  **Slow Roast the Lamb:** Preheat your oven to a low temperature, around 300°F (150°C). Place the marinated lamb in a large roasting pan. If using, scatter the quartered onions and chopped carrots around the lamb. Pour 2 cups of broth into the bottom of the pan. Cover the roasting pan tightly with foil or a lid. Roast for 4-6 hours, or until the lamb is incredibly tender and easily pulls away from the bone. The exact time will depend on the size of your lamb and your oven. For the last 30-45 minutes, remove the foil to allow the lamb to brown and crisp up slightly. Once done, remove the lamb from the oven, transfer it to a carving board, tent loosely with foil, and let it rest for at least 20-30 minutes. This resting period is crucial for juicy meat.

3.  **Prepare the Aromatic Spiced Rice:** While the lamb is resting, prepare the rice. Melt butter or ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the whole spices (cardamom pods, bay leaves, cinnamon stick) and ground spices (cumin, coriander, allspice, turmeric, cinnamon) and cook for another minute until fragrant. Add the rinsed basmati rice and stir to coat evenly with the spices. Pour in the broth and add salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender. If using, stir in the frozen peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Let the rice stand, covered, for 5 minutes off the heat before fluffing with a fork.

4.  **Assemble and Serve:** On a large serving platter, create a generous bed of the aromatic spiced rice. Carefully carve or shred the tender Lamb Ouzi, arranging the pieces beautifully over the rice. Drizzle some of the pan juices from the roasted lamb over the meat and rice for extra flavor. Garnish generously with the toasted nuts and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately and watch your guests marvel at this stunning Middle Eastern dinner recipe.

## Tips for Perfectly Slow Roasted Lamb

Achieving that melt-in-your-mouth tenderness for your whole slow roasted lamb is key to a successful Ouzi. Here are a few tips:

*   **Marinate generously:** Don't rush the marination process. The longer the lamb sits in the spice mixture, the more flavor it will absorb. Overnight is truly best.
*   **Low and Slow is the Way to Go:** Resist the urge to crank up the heat. A low oven temperature (around 300°F / 150°C) over several hours is what breaks down the connective tissues, resulting in incredibly tender meat.
*   **Keep it Covered:** Covering the roasting pan tightly with foil or a lid traps steam, helping to keep the lamb moist and tender throughout the long cooking process. Only uncover towards the end to get a nice brown crust.
*   **Rest the Meat:** This is non-negotiable! Resting allows the juices to redistribute throughout the meat, ensuring every bite is succulent. Skipping this step will result in dry lamb.
*   **Use Bone-In Lamb:** The bone adds significant flavor to the lamb as it roasts, contributing to a richer overall taste for your Lamb Ouzi.

## Serving Suggestions for Lamb Ouzi

Lamb Ouzi is a feast in itself, but a few complementary side dishes can elevate the experience and balance the rich flavors.

*   **Cooling Yogurt Sauce:** A simple cucumber and mint yogurt sauce (similar to tzatziki) provides a refreshing contrast to the rich lamb and spiced rice.
*   **Fresh Salads:** A vibrant Fattoush or Tabbouleh salad adds freshness, crunch, and a tangy counterpoint. The bright herbs and vegetables cut through the richness beautifully.
*   **Pickles:** Assorted Middle Eastern pickles, such as pickled turnips or cucumbers, offer a zesty and briny element that complements the meal.
*   **Warm Pita Bread:** Essential for scooping up every last bit of the delicious lamb and rice.
*   **Mint Tea:** A traditional ending to a Middle Eastern meal, offering a refreshing digestif.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the traditional Lamb Ouzi recipe is a masterpiece, feel free to explore variations to suit your taste or available ingredients.

*   **Different Cuts of Lamb:** While a whole leg or shoulder is traditional, you can adapt the recipe for smaller cuts like lamb shanks or even bone-in chops, adjusting cooking times accordingly.
*   **Spice Adjustments:** Feel free to modify the spice blend. Add a pinch of sumac for tang, or a touch of ground cloves for deeper warmth. Za'atar can also be a wonderful addition to the lamb marinade.
*   **Rice Additions:** Beyond peas, consider adding sautéed carrots, chickpeas, or even diced potatoes to the rice pilaf for extra texture and flavor.
*   **Dried Fruit:** Some regional variations include dried apricots or raisins in the rice for a touch of sweetness that pairs beautifully with the savory lamb.
*   **Stuffing the Lamb:** For an even more elaborate presentation, some recipes involve partially deboning the lamb leg and stuffing it with a mixture of spiced rice, nuts, and ground meat before roasting.

## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

**Q: Can I make Lamb Ouzi ahead of time?**
A: The lamb can be slow roasted a day in advance. Once cooked, let it cool, then shred or slice and store in an airtight container with some of its pan juices. Reheat gently in the oven or microwave. The rice is best made fresh, but you can prepare it a few hours ahead and gently reheat, fluffing with a fork before serving.

**Q: What cut of lamb is best for whole slow roasted Ouzi?**
A: A bone-in leg of lamb or lamb shoulder is highly recommended. The bone adds significant flavor, and these cuts have enough fat and connective tissue to become incredibly tender and moist during the long, slow roasting process.

**Q: How long does it take to slow roast a 5-7 pound leg of lamb?**
A: Typically, a 5-7 pound bone-in leg of lamb will take approximately 4-6 hours at 300°F (150°C) when covered. The exact time depends on your oven and the lamb's starting temperature and size. The key is to roast until it's fall-off-the-bone tender, not just to a specific internal temperature.

**Q: Can I use a pressure cooker for the lamb instead of slow roasting?**
A: While a pressure cooker can significantly reduce cooking time for the lamb, it won't replicate the same depth of flavor or the beautiful crust that develops with slow roasting. For an authentic and superior Lamb Ouzi experience, slow roasting is highly recommended.

Creating a whole slow roasted Lamb Ouzi is a rewarding culinary endeavor that promises a truly unforgettable meal. The tender, aromatic lamb, paired with fragrant spiced rice, creates a harmony of flavors that speaks of tradition, generosity, and exquisite taste. This Middle Eastern dinner recipe is a testament to the magic that happens when simple, quality ingredients are treated with patience and care. Gather your loved ones, prepare this magnificent dish, and let the rich flavors transport you to a world of culinary delight.
